utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please sit down. I'd remind you of the affirmation you made to tell the truth which still applies. Now, Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Stalevic.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: We'll continue where we left off yesterday. My last question to you and your last answer yesterday were related to the information you received from Mr. Trajkovic, about his contacts with the gentleman called Mrgud, and the information that he had passed to Djordjevic, namely the fact that the minister's decision was being awaited about the admission of those men. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: While we were waiting for the minister's decision to admit these men into the reserve force, it became already certain that the NATO aggression was going forward and it indeed began on the 23rd and the 24th, and our unit was at that moment relocated for the purposes of our next assignment in the area of Kursumlija heading for Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: What about that reserve force of the MUP, was it seconded to your unit?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you explain to us what happened, why wasn't it seconded, and how the situation developed from the beginning of the NATO aggression?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the beginning of the NATO aggression, we went forward with the operation that had been planned for that period and we set out after passing Krpina village we reached Bradas village, and as we arrived there we stopped to link up our units. On the 26th in the evening, Trajkovic left. I don't know where. It was 10.00 or 11.00, I'm not sure when Trajkovic called me on the radio and told me to wait for him on the road leading from Podujevo via Krpina village towards Bradas. I took my car with the driver and Dr. Markovic and went down to the road. The Krpina-Podujevo road, and my car went ahead of the commander's vehicle. In that other vehicle there were the commander, his driver, and some other persons. Some 50 to 60 metres from the place from which I started to meet him, I saw in the rear view mirror an explosion, and I heard the explosion, and I saw thick black smoke. I stopped immediately, got out of my car, and I saw that the vehicle driving behind me, the vehicle of my commander Trajkovic was there. Dr. Markovic got out of the car with me. And I saw the commander lying by the road in some gully filled with water. I approached to see what was wrong with him. He said his neck was hurting, he was injured, and next to him there was Zoran Basrak, member of the special unit, and Nikola Pedovic [phoen] an analyst working with Mr. Trajkovic and Radovan Aleksic who had been the driver of Commander Trajkovic. The doctor started administering first aid immediately first to Radovan Aleksic but then he realised the man was dead. After that we organised transport for our injured colleagues and the commander to the Pristina hospital for a check-up and transport for the body of Radovan Aleksic to the forensic department of the hospital for a postmortem. When they left for Pristina, I was called by Dragan Markovic, my physician, saying that Mr. Trajkovic had light injuries and that he would go to the MUP staff in Pristina for combatting terrorism.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Before we go on, let's clarify one thing. When you talk about the time between 10.00 and 11.00 saying that Trajkovic called you on the radio and told you to meet him on the road leading from Podujevo via Krpina village towards Bradas, what date was it?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your question was not quite precise. Trajkovic called us on our own radio communication. It was 10.00, 11.00 in the morning. It was not the Pristina-Bradas road, it was between Krpina and Bradas. On the 26th, Trajkovic left to go somewhere, and the incident I described was on the 27th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Could you now tell us what happened after you received this information about the injuries to Commander Trajkovic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was told that he was only lightly injured and that he would be able to go to the staff, on the same day, the 27th, Trajkovic and the doctor Dragan Markovic returned to the police department of Podujevo, which was located just outside Podujevo. He came and told us that he had been at the staff and that the staff had decided that the reserve unit from Prolom Banja would join us in Podujevo, and he ordered Simovic, commander of the special anti-terrorist unit Belgrade, to go and to reach an agreement and make arrangements about bringing that reserve unit of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: We need to clarify something for the record. This police department OUP Podujevo, where was it at that moment?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 27th when we arrived from Bradas, the OUP Podujevo had been relocated from its normal peacetime location and it was -- its new location was close by to its normal peacetime location. I as the commander of the SAJ came to that new location of the OUP, that's where our headquarters was.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: To be quite precise, this new location was in Podujevo itself?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 50, 70 metres from the normal location of OUP Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: We had to clarify because it was not quite clear in the record. Tell me about that meeting you had with Trajkovic after he returned to Podujevo on the 27th. What exactly did Trajkovic tell you and Simovic at that meeting?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, on that day, that afternoon on the 27th when he came, he said he had received approval from the MUP staff to bring in this reserve force of the MUP the next day, that is the 28th. He instructed Simovic to go to Prolom Banja and agree about bringing in that reserve force of the MUP to Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did he instruct Simovic to make contact with anyone in Prolom Banja who would be the contact person for bringing these people?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was present at that meeting when the commander, Mr. Trajkovic, gave instructions to Simovic to go to Prolom Banja and to look for one certain Slobodan Medic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Now, tell us what happened next. Did Commander Trajkovic remain in Podujevo?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, he did not remain in Podujevo that evening because his own driver had been killed, he told us that he would go to organise the funeral of the late Aleksic, and then he set out for Belgrade. And Simovic also left at the same time with him because it was in the same direction, Belgrade and this hotel in Prolom Banja where these reservists were accommodated. We are talking still about the 27th March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did ultimately members of the reserve force arrive in Podujevo and how?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 27th Simovic went to talk to them in Prolom Banja, and on that day they did not arrive. Simovic went again the next day, the 28th, to Prolom Banja, and brought them in the morning of the 28th.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you when the reservists arrived?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When this reserve force of the MUP arrived, I was in this new location of OUP Podujevo very close to the normal location of the OUP, and I was there with Dr. Dragan Markovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And what happened next?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After awhile, Simovic, the commander of the Belgrade SAJ came to that new location of the OUP and there was with him an unfamiliar person who introduced himself as Boca. They came into the headquarters and they sat down with me there, and Dr. Markovic was still there. And 30 minutes or so later we heard short volleys of automatic fire. And then I don't remember any more who ran out first, was it Dr. Markovic or was it Simovic, but they ran out of the building of the headquarters, and we ran out towards the place where these volleys had come from. I remained in the headquarters, together with this man Boca. I don't know whether there was anyone still there, but Boca and I remained at the headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: At that time did you know what was happening and what was this all about?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know what was happening, but through radio communication, I heard that there were injured people. Shortly thereafter when we heard there were injured people through radio communication, Dr. Dragan Markovic called me and told me that there were injured civilians, and that they should be transported to hospital to receive medical assistance. I gave my vehicle and my driver sent to the place where assistance was needed, and I organised the transport of these civilians to a hospital in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Where were you during all this time that you are talking about?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on the premises of this staff, which was in the close proximity of the OUP, as I said, 50 to 70 metres. And with me there was this person called Boca. So that was the OUP premises where the staff was accommodated.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. What happened next?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After some 30 or 40 minutes, Commander Simovic came to the staff premises and instructed Boca, this person Boca, to go towards Podujevo to put people on the buses and to return them to Prolom Banja from where they had come. As soon as they boarded the buses, Simovic went together with them from Podujevo towards Prolom Banja.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Can we just go back a little. When Simovic arrived in the office where you and Boca were, what did he tell you?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Simovic told Boca that members of this MUP reserve force had killed some civilians and that my Dr. Markovic went there to offer them assistance, and because of that he shouted at Boca and told him to get on the buses and to go back from where they had come from. As soon as he came in and after he told Boca to get on the bus and return his men back, while I was still there at the OUP command post, before that, as soon as he came in he reported this to the police station, or rather, the person who was in charge of that OUP. After that, after he had decided to send the reserve forces back, he informed the MUP staff for terrorism -- anti-terrorism in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, what happened after that, or rather, at that moment, did you know how many people had been injured?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After these men boarded the buses and Simovic sent Medic back, Dr. Markovic came to the staff headquarters where I was. He told me that he had took care of those wounded people and that he had transported them, but he also told me that there had been killed people as a result of this crime, but he didn't tell me how many. At that point we left our personnel to secure the crime scene since we notified the OUP Podujevo about the crime, and they were expected to arrange for an on-site investigation, that is to say, to summon an investigation judge and carry out all the procedures that were prescribed in such situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: In your unit, did you have scene-of-crime technicians or any other qualified personnel who were capable of carrying out an on-site investigation?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special anti-terrorist unit had never been involved in crime scene investigations or other investigations of that kind. That was an elite unit that was intended for completely different tasks. We never had a person qualified to carry out this kind of investigation because that was the duty of investigating organs, and it was up to them to arrange this investigation.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: After this incident, did you do anything to establish whether any members of your unit had been involved in it?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I -- after we sent this notification to the OUP and the officer in charge there so that they could carry out the on-site investigation, I lined up my men and also the men from Belgrade after Tetinac had left, and I asked both groups whether any of them committed this crime or if they had seen the perpetrators. They answered that they hadn't committed any crimes and they hadn't seen who had done it. After that I instructed the platoon commanders to check the status of weapons of my members and the members of the Belgrade special unit. They did so, and they told me that they all had their combat sets that had issued to me. We call it BK, that's a combat kit which contains certain number of ammunition, and each bullet was registered with the police officer who had issued it.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 28th of March, did your unit remain in Podujevo, or was it given a new assignment?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it did not remain in Podujevo. They were given a new assignment on the 28th, and I and both units went to Kosovo Polje, and one part went to Kosovska Gracanica which was close to my base.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stalevic, it is obvious that on the 28th of March, the research forces of the MUP were not attached to your unit. During combat operations in Kosovo until the 29th of June, 1999, was reserve force ever attached to your unit, the reserve forces of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sometime in the second half or towards the end of April the reserve force of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia was attached to the special anti-terrorist unit of the MUP of Republic of Serbia, and they remained there until the 9th or 10th of May, if I'm not mistaken. So in total some 10 days starting from the date when they join us towards the end of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you describe to us the circumstances under which this happened?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had daily actions in that particular period, and we went from one action to another. One day Zivko Trajkovic went to the staff premises and asked for the reserve forces to be re-introduced. That was granted by the staff, and after that they were engaged through the police administration, or rather, approval was given for the reserve MUP forces to be attached to us in Kosovo Polje. As I saw that happen towards the end of that month and they came to Kosovo Polje, they were brought then by Commander Trajkovic, and after that, after we had billeted them in Kosovo Polje the commander issued tasks, issued to me and the then-commander of the Belgrade SAJ Simovic, or rather, attached these men that had been sent from the MUP, from their reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: These members of the reserve force that were attached to your unit at the end of April, did they have any connection with the people who were in Podujevo on the 28th of March?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: No, I didn't know whether they had any connections with the men who were in Podujevo on the 28th of March.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All I know is that Commander Trajkovic said then that these reserve forces would be screened and that he would personally guarantee for the execution of the tasks when they become attached to our unit in Kosovo Polje.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please describe, once these reserve forces came to Kosovo Polje, how they were attached to your unit and placed under your command and control.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These members of the MUP reserve forces were first billeted in Kosovo Polje and the commander [microphone not activated] these men to Mr. Simovic and me. I held a meeting with them, I asked them about their military specialties, and according to that, I fitted them into my unit. On that occasion they were mostly used to secure our facilities and the flanks of our units, that is to say, the lines reached after we had carried these actions in 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, in what way did these reserve forces carry out the tasks that you gave them?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When they arrived at the end of April, they carried out these tasks together with us in a professional and responsible way during the ten days of their engagement.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In 1999 were you aware of the fact that members of the reserve forces that were attached to your unit, or did you know that they had committed any crimes in the wars that were waged in the former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: In 1999, did you know that members of the MUP reserve forces attached to your unit carried out any crimes in the former Yugoslavia before that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't know anything about that in 1999 to the effect that members of the MUP had carried out or committed any crimes in the territory of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stalevic, are you acquainted with General Vlastimir Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that General Djordjevic was the head of the department, or rather, the assistant minister of MUP of Republika Serbia. I used to see him but I was not acquainted with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: How many times have you seen, if you have seen, Mr. Djordjevic during 1998?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him a few times in 1998. A few times.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Can you perhaps remember when? I know it was a long time ago, I'm not looking for an exact date.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I think I saw him when in 1998 we carried out actions and we entered Malisevo. I also believe that I saw him during the liberation of the road that had been blocked, the road between Pristina and Komorane, or rather, Pec. And I also think that I saw him once in 1998 at Cicavica when we carried an action of crashing the Siptar terrorist groups. At the foot of that mountain there was a group of refugees of Albanian Siptar civilians. I reached the place where those refugees were. Those were the people who were trying to escape combat operations that were carried out both by the Siptar terrorists and our army. Dr. Dragan Markovic was constantly with me, came and asked me for a vehicle to be used to transport a heavily pregnant woman to Pristina. I gave this vehicle to the doctor, and he took this woman to Pristina hospital. The women and children who were there were given food and water by us as of much as we could afford to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: While we are on the subject, tell us about how the special anti-terrorist unit treated civilians whom they encountered in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were completely professional and official apart from situations like the one I just described. We had no contact with civilians in places where there were Siptar terrorists, where they offered resistance, we carried out operations against them. And I'm now talking about the special anti-terrorist unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to go back now to the role of General Djordjevic in 1998 when you saw him on the locations where you saw him. Do you know what his role was?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the course of 1998, or rather, the second half of 1998 when we were in combat against Siptar terrorists, he would come to see the troops if we needed any assistance, rest, or food. He did not have a command role whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Did Mr. Djordjevic at any time give you any order in that period?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Djordjevic never gave me any orders. I was given orders by my own commander, Zivko Trajkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: And were you present, did you hear, or did you see him give any kind of order whatsoever to Zivko Trajkovic related to the operations you were carrying out in KiM?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, I was never aware of something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever see Vlastimir Djordjevic in 1999, specifically from the beginning of combat operations until the end of June 1999? And if so, when?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw him once in 1999, at least I think it was in 1999. And that was on the 15th, or rather, 16th January. There was a session of the government being held in Pristina and the chief of sector attended so that members of my unit provided security to the members of the leadership who attended, and on the 15th, or rather, the 16th, he called me in the afternoon saying that he needed to go to Mount Kopaonik for skiing, on a skiing trip. I offered my help. I said I could organise it but that I wanted to go too because I had worked as a ski instructor in special units. So I provided an escort vehicle from my unit to go to Zvecani which is just after Mitrovica, and that afternoon, the chief of sector and I set out with this escort. At Zvecani the escort left us and turned back, and we went on to Mount Kopaonik. We skied there the next day, and around noon he got a call on his cell phone and told me Sava, look, something cropped up, the situation in Kosovo and Metohija got complicated. They will send a helicopter to fetch me. You go on skiing, and if need be, they will call you too. So that was on the 17th when he left. I stayed on for some more skiing, and soon afterwards, I went back. I was met by a vehicle at Zvecani, and I went back to my base at Ajvalija. That was the night of the 17th.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. After that day, the 17th of January until combat operations were finished on the 10th of June, did you see him again in Kosovo or anywhere in the territory of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that was the one time when I saw him, and the day when we were skiing together.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Stalevic, at any time in 1998 or 1999 did you hear or see that there was any plan within the Ministry of the Interior to expel the ethnic Albanian population from the territory of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen any kind of plan to expel the Albanian population, either in 1998 or 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: In 1998 or 1999, did you ever hear or see that there was any plan or understanding within the Ministry of the Interior in order to expel the Albanian population and thus change the ethnic composition of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I've never seen anything like that. I never heard about it or seen anything of the kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Stalevic. Your Honours, I've finished my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Popovic. Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: My name is Eliott Behar. I'm counsel for the Prosecution, and I'll have some questions for you this morning. Sir, I want to start by asking you some very basic questions about the incident that took place in Podujevo. Now, I take it that you are well aware as of today of how serious this massacre was. There were 19 people who were killed, at least a dozen women and young children were machine-gunned in a group against a wall, and there were five survivors, each of whom was a child and several of whom were grievously injured. Is that something, sir, that you are now aware of?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a rather long question. I knew at the time because the doctor went there and came back and told me, I knew that there were people injured and that they had been given assistance and they were later transported to the hospital in Pristina. The doctor also told me that some people were dead. He didn't tell me how many dead. I learned later about what you mentioned in this very long question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, sir, I take it that this event would have been particularly memorable for you, and that you would certainly remember where you were and who you were with when this incident took place; is that fair to say?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that incident when it happened, I was at the headquarters not far from the OUP Podujevo. I was on the premises of the headquarters with Boca, Slobodan Medic, when the incident occurred. I was not right there on the spot.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Let me go through this because I want to make sure I have this exactly right. You are saying you were at the headquarters. Were you at the location of the OUP Podujevo itself?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was at the headquarters of OU Podujevo which had been relocated from its peacetime location. It was relocated to another location very close by to the normal location 50, 70 metres away. That's where I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And at that time, the time that the shooting occurred, it seems to me we have a couple already different versions of who you were with. Who exactly were you with, sir, in the OUP Podujevo building at the time the shooting took place?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The correct version is this, when we heard those two volleys of fire, at the headquarters at the OUP Podujevo, there was I, Dr. Markovic, Zoran Simovic, and this man Boca. I can't remember exactly if anyone was -- anyone else was there, but the four of us were certainly there when we heard those volleys of fire.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And so when just earlier you said I was on the premises of the headquarters with Boca, Slobodan Medic, you didn't mention anyone else, did you just forget at that time to mention Mr. Simovic and Dragan Markovic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am unable to follow the transcript or the interpretation, but on that day I was at the headquarters with this man Boca, whose name is Slobodan Medic. Afterwards, Simovic came with this man Boca, that's how he introduced himself when he came in, just Boca.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay. Let me just explain this. Before we go on, sir, if there's anything that you don't understand in the translation that you are receiving or in something that's said, please let me know, we'll rephrase it. I want to make sure that we are on the same page. Now, again, and right now you have just mentioned Simovic came in with this man Boca. Just to be absolutely clear, your position is that you were at the OUP headquarters at the time the firing took place with Mr. Simovic; with Boca, Slobodan Medic; and with Dragan Markovic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Dragan and I were at the headquarters. We were there. After awhile, Simovic arrived together with Slobodan Medic, and from the moment of their arrival, 30 minutes afterwards, we heard this shooting.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I think that's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we can see Exhibit 06117, please. I'll just indicate, Your Honours, there are -- these are documents within the 65 ter numbers that contain several statements, so when I call them up I'll be asking for the specific statement, and I think I'll propose to tender them at the end once I've dealt with several of the statements already. I hope it doesn't get too complicated. But I'm looking for -- the English translation would be K054-6763, and in B/C/S, I'll need page 11.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall giving an interview on the 3rd of April, 2002 to the district court in Prokuplje? This is a record of that interview on the screen.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that. I remember I was at Prokuplje and that I gave this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we can see the next page in the English and the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, here, sir, you say starting from the second line, if we could just zoom in a little bit. "On the 28th of March, 1999, I was quartered in a house in Podujevo near the Podujevo OUP, and Dr. Markovic was with me. While we were sitting there, the doctor was called via radio communications to go urgently to the place from where they were calling. He left immediately and I remained in the house." Do you recall saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember, Mr. Prosecutor, this interview, and I remember also making the statement that Dragan Markovic and Zoran Simovic were with me in the OUP headquarters and also Boca, but in this statement here it says I was with Dr. Markovic. When I was giving this statement, I spoke to the investigating judge for about 20, 30 minutes about the incident itself, and after that, the judge started dictating a statement for the record and said that it would be quite sufficient otherwise the statement would have been too long, and he extracted only the main elements considering that I was not a direct participant of the incident.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: But you will agree with me, sir, that in that statement there is no mention of Mr. Simovic, there's no mention of Boca, and, in fact, you are not even at the OUP, you are in a house. Do you agree with me, sir, that this statement is different from the account that you just gave us?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, Mr. Prosecutor, I was giving a statement about who was at that headquarters. The headquarters was moved to a new location not far away. Apart from me and Dragan, there was Simovic and Boca and then when I was in Prokuplje, I was also saying this same thing, but the Prosecutor there said that there was no need for all that to be reflected in the statement, it would make the statement too long, and I agreed and I signed the statement I gave then, and it's correct and truthful, the statement I gave then.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I'm not too concerned with the length of this statement, what I'm concerned with is that it provides a materially different state of fact. And that is, in fact, your statement -- pardon me, your signature at the bottom of this statement, is it not?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is my signature, but I only gave a statement insofar as the Prosecutor was asking questions and I said what I knew. And the investigating judge said it was quite enough. I agreed with him and I signed that statement, and it's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I think we have that position, sir. Let's move on and look at something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we can look at 06118, please. And here in the English I'll need K054-6915. B/C/S if we could have page 36. I'm not sure that that is the right statement in English. Let me just have a moment's indulgence. It's page 14 in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So if we can look here, sir, at the final paragraph in English starting from the second line, I'll read from, you say: "On the critical day, the 28th of March, 1999, I was in Podujevo. As I was a member of another unit, I was objectively in no position or at the scene, nor did I see what happened, but the moment I was informed that some people had been hurt, I gave my doctor my vehicle, and my driver and I ordered taking all measures to help the wounded." Do you recall saying that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says, yes, commander of the special unit in Pristina on the day, 28th March, 1999, I was in Podujevo. I was a member of another unit. Yes, I was a member of another unit. I'm from the special anti-terrorist unit, I'm not from the reserve force of the MUP. And I was, therefore, from another unit. The regular unit of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. That's not the part I'm concerned with.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I was --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: What I'm concerned with is your statement that you were informed that some people had been hurt and that at that point you gave your doctor -- you gave the doctor your vehicle, and that you ordered taking all measures to help the wounded. I'm asking you if you recall saying that.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just saying it says here that I'm from another unit, and I was indeed from another unit because those men were the reserve force of the MUP. And as for this other part that I provided a doctor to go to the scene, I did provide a doctor to go and give assistance to the people at the scene. I was asked to provide a vehicle and assistance to be given to the injured people. But I'm stating with full responsibility that I had not seen this statement or signed it as such. I know what I said, but I don't know what was written. I didn't have time to read what was written there. I'm saying the same thing then as now, that we were not from the same unit because they were a reserve unit, and that I sent a doctor to give assistance to the injured and that a vehicle was asked from me to transport them to the Pristina hospital, that's true, I did provide that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I think we have your position, sir. I can tell you this is a record of your court appearance. So it's not a statement. This one is not a statement, this is what you said in court. But I can see, sir, it says right on the top of that same page that you took an oath. Do you recall taking an oath just as you took one here to tell the truth in court?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was telling the truth then, and I'm telling the truth now, but I don't know at this trial what they were writing. I didn't have time or opportunity to read it, and I'm stating with full responsibility again that we were not from the same unit. I am from the special anti-terrorist unit of the MUP, and they were from the reserve force of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I know that, sir. That's not contentious. It's not at issue here. My point was that once again then, and I am certain that you took an oath to tell the whole truth, at no point did you mention Mr. Simovic, at no point did you mention Boca. Once again on that account you were just with the doctor. Sir, let me move on.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this statement that I'm looking at, I didn't mention it, but as I said, this refers to this MUP reserve forces when I say that we were not member of the same unit. I never looked at this statement, I didn't read it, and I didn't sign it. I did give a statement though, and I know I did that when I attended this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, what I find interesting is that when you gave this version of where you were, there were other witnesses who corroborated your account at the same time. And I'd like to take you through that and give you a chance to comment. Now, sir, you, Dragan Markovic, and Zoran Simovic all gave statements on the same day, the 3rd of April, 2002. Do you recall that? I'll just ask you, do you recall giving a statement on the same day as Dragan Markovic and Zoran Simovic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I was on that day at the Prokuplje court, that I gave a statement about this incident. They were there probably, but I cannot remember with any degree of certainty that they were there on the same day. I know that I was there in Prokuplje on that date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we could see 06117, please. And in the English it's K054-6753.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, sir, I want to take a look at the statement that was given by the doctor you've mentioned, Dragan Markovic, who you said that you were with. If we look at page 2 in the B/C/S and the English. If we look at the second paragraph, and it is the, I believe it's the third line. I'll start reading at the third line. Dr. Markovic said: "Our group included Stalevic, the commander of the Pristina special unit. After awhile, you could hear one - at least, I think that is what happened - long burst of fire." Now, Dr. Markovic, so he has already said he is with you -- sorry, are you having trouble seeing that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't find that particular portion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: It should be in the second paragraph there, sir. You see a line that says, "our group included Stalevic..." if you can find your name on the page?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I have found it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: He says: "Our group included Stalevic, the commander of the Pristina special unit. After awhile you could hear one - at least, I think that is what happened - long burst of fire." Now, if you continue on to the last sentence in the paragraph, Dr. Markovic says: "The burst of fire that could be heard was nearby, and after five minutes, I was called over radio communication by the SAJ Belgrade Commander Simovic to urgently come to the building near the municipal centre because there was some need for my intervention." Do you see that part, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So it's clear from this version of events, sir, that you and Dr. Markovic are together as you said in your initial statement, and that you are in a different place from Mr. Simovic because Dr. Markovic has said that Mr. Simovic called him on the radio. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see this statement. At the time I was not far away of the headquarters of the original -- there was Dragan Markovic as well and Simovic and Boca joined us later. So approximately 30 or 45 minutes later we heard short bursts of fire. I don't know who went out first, but then I heard on the radio communication --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. We have that, sir, and that's fine. I'm talking about the moment of the shooting, and that's mentioned in this statement. But I want to take you through something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we can look at Mr. Simovic's statement. This is again 06117. The English is K054-6753. Actually, that may be the same one. Sorry, 6756, please. It's page 4 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So, sir, we can see this is indeed the same date, April 3rd, 2002. This is Mr. Simovic's statement. And if you look at the next page in English and B/C/S. If you look at the fourth paragraph in B/C/S, sir, and in English we can look at the final paragraph. There's a single line there that says -- sorry, it's just before -- in English it's the line just before the final paragraph. Mr. Simovic says: "I went to the command post, i.e., the 'staff,' with Boca and some of his men." So there Mr. Simovic didn't say anything about you. On this version you are not with Mr. Simovic at the staff. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please point this precise portion to me. I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I believe it's the fourth paragraph in B/C/S from the top. It's directly, if you see --

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here where it says, "I went to the town command i.e., the headquarters with Boca and some other men," is that what you are referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When Boca came and also Zoran Simovic, I was at the headquarters which was not far away from the OUP, and I was there the whole time. So my statement that I made about my being at the OUP headquarters, I can categorically confirm that I was there at the time when Simovic and Boca came. I don't remember about these other men. I know that Simovic and Boca came, and I know that for certain. And I also know that Markovic was there. I'm not sure whether anyone else was there, but I'm sure about the four of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, we've seen three versions now, yours, Mr. Simovic's version, Dragan Markovic's version, all of this having the same state of affairs of you being with the doctor and not with Mr. Simovic. Let me be very direct about what I'm suggesting, sir, because I want to give you a chance to respond. I'm going to suggest that you and Mr. Simovic and Dr. Markovic and perhaps others participated in a coverup in 2002 when you provided this testimony. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not carrying out any cover-up. I claim with full responsibility, and I did that then and I'm doing it now, that I was at the headquarters, that Simovic was there as well. And I didn't attempt to do any cover-up. When Markovic called me and told me that there were injured people, I gave him a vehicle to transport them to Pristina. So there was no cover-up.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine. And let me just be clear, sir. I have your position now on where you were, what I'm trying to focus on is what you said in 2002. Let me get your comment on another exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: P493. If we can see page 13 in the English and page 14 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, these statements and this testimony surrounds what took place at the Prokuplje court. Do you recall that Goran Stoparic also testified at the Cvjetan trial at the Prokuplje district Court, the same trial that you are giving statements for?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Prokuplje at the time, but I don't remember this person giving a statement. I don't know which name you mentioned, Goran something. All I know is that I gave a statement on that day and I returned immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I'd like to focus on what he said here, if we look at paragraph 83, if we can just scroll down in the English slightly. Now, in the second line, sorry, it's the -- starting from the third line into paragraph 83, Mr. Stoparic explains this: "The first time, or the first trial, was in Prokuplje district court. I was approached by the lead Defence lawyer for Sasa, Zarko Kalanj, who wanted me to help Sasa. I was provided with a statement already written out. This statement was not true." My question for you is this, sir: Were you approached by that lawyer or by anyone else and asked to conspire to cover up the truth with respect to that massacre and with respect to your evidence?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I did was give statement. Nobody approached me. I gave it of my own volition, and nobody approached me on that day. I answered the questions asked by the judge, and I described the incident. Therefore, no one approached me in the sense that you are implying.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we can just quickly look at the next page in English, it's the same page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we can look at paragraph 84, here, sir, you just mentioned your testimony, Mr. Stoparic said: "When I was called to give evidence I said that I could not remember. This is how I answered all the questions. I was afraid to tell the truth to the court." Then he says: "Everyone that gave evidence lied in order to help Sasa." Is that true, sir, did you lie in order to help Sasa, and were you aware of anyone else at the time lying in order to protect Sasa?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, I don't know what this Stoparic person said. As far as I'm concerned, I can categorically say that I never told a lie. I told only what I knew about what happened on the 28th in response to the questions that I had been asked. I didn't lie either then or now. I'm telling you the truth about this incident, this massacre that took place on the 28th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see we are nearing the break and I suspect that the next set of things I need to show the witness may take a little longer than five minutes. If it's convenient I can break now or I'm happy to press through as best I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If it's going to be more practical, we will break now. It's only five minutes. We will adjourn and resume at five minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, when we left off last time we looked at a set of statements from the 3rd of April, 2002, which had a state of affairs in which you were with the doctor at the time that the massacre took place. I'd like to take you through what I say is another version with respect to where you were at the time of the massacre.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we could see Exhibit 06108, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, this is a statement that you gave to the MUP Working Group on the 15th of February, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And if we can look at the second page in English. Just scroll down a bit in B/C/S. If we can have the next page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So if we look here, sir, at the third paragraph down I'll start. Here you say: "I attended a meeting in the Podujevo OUP where the units accommodation and manner of engagement were discussed." Then you say: "In addition to me, the following were present at the meeting: Commanders of units, engaged in the Podujevo area, a representative of the MUP staff; Zoran Simovic, commander of the Belgrade SAJ; and Boca. While the meeting was in progress I heard to bursts of automatic fire. After that, Zoran Simovic went out to see what was going on." Do you recall saying that, sir? And just to be clear, I'm not asking you what happened, I'm just asking you if you remember saying that in 2002?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, on that day when this happened, I was present at the meeting at the headquarters relocated in Podujevo not far away. Also present at this meeting were Commander Simovic, Boca, and the doctor. I don't remember anyone else being in attendance, as I said before.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Let me point stop you. I'm trying to be as clear as I can. I'm not asking you about what happened. I think you've been very clear in repeating what you say happened that day. I'm just asking you with respect to this statement that's on the screen, I'm asking you if you remembered giving that statement on the 15th of February, 2002? Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I gave that statement. I didn't remember when this was exactly, but I can see it here, and you can see that this statement was taken by a Working Group of the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And if we can just look at the next page in English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Is that your signature, sir, at the bottom of the page there, really in the middle of the page?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Would you agree with me, sir, that the doctor is not mentioned as being with you in this statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can claim with full responsibility now and I did so then when I made the statement, that Dr. Markovic was with us at this meeting. As far as I can see here, this Working Group that took those statements for the record from us didn't sign it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: But you signed it, sir. You signed it to confirm that it was accurate; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The statement is accurate about what I'm talking about, and that is to say that present at the meeting was the doctor, that he was there, that SAJ Commander Simovic came, and that Boca also joined the meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, was that statement that you gave on the 15th of February, 2002, was that your evidence, or did someone else write that out for you or tell you to say that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You mean this statement that we are looking at right now?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Yes, just talking about this specific statement. I'm asking you, did you go there and give your own evidence independently, or did someone else write that out or tell you to say that on your behalf?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they just came to take a statement, this Working Group. Nobody had written anything or told me anything. I said what I'm repeating now, and what is written here was actually compiled by them. As I said, the doctor, myself, Simovic, and Boca were at the meeting on the 28th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And just so we are entirely clear, sir, did you collaborate with anyone else, and what I mean by that is, did you speak to any other witnesses about what your evidence should be before you gave that statement?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never discussed anything with any other witnesses as you are indicated. No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: What I find interesting, sir, and I'll give you a chance to look at it, is that in some respects, this statement is, in my submission, almost identical to what Mr. Simovic said.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we can see P1590, please. In fact, before I move on, Your Honours, I would seek to tender that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: This is the statement of the present witness now on the screen?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's correct. And it's the only statement under that 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit P01597.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So if we could see now P1590, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, you can see that this is the statement of Mr. Simovic, you can see from the date there it was given on the same day, the 15th of February, 2002.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And if we can stay on the same page in B/C/S but look at page 2 in English. Perhaps just zoom in to the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: In the third paragraph down, sir, Mr. Simovic said: "The following were present at the meeting in the Podujevo OUP: Commanders of units engaged in the Podujevo area; a representative of the MUP staff; Radislav Stalevic, commander of the SAJ Pristina; and Boca. While the meeting was in progress, I heard two bursts of automatic fire and rushed outside to see what was going on." Are you able to explain that similarity, sir, not just in the content but in the wording of the statement to what you had said?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I should not like to explain this. Simovic gave in statement and signed it as his own. I didn't discuss with anyone how to give my statement, and again, I can only state with full responsibility that I was at that meeting with Markovic, Simovic, and this Boca. I don't remember clearly whether anyone else was present on that day on the 28th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: This interview, sir, on the 15th of February, 2002, do you recall where it took place?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That interview when I was giving this statement I think, if I'm not mistaken, because I'm not completely sure, I think it was at the command of the gendarmerie somewhere in Belgrade. That's where the gendarmerie of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia is based.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, we can see that if you scroll up to the top of the document, it indicates that. In fact, at that time, sir, both you and Mr. Simovic were employed working for the gendarmerie, were you not?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that yesterday, in 2001 I started working with the gendarmerie as assistant commander of the gendarmerie of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, and in 2002 at some point I transferred to a unit that had been newly formed, the Novi Sad gendarmerie detachment. And it's true that I gave a statement at the command of the gendarmerie because my detachment was at that time in Novi Sad. It was set up sometime in 2002. I can't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine, sir. That's going beyond my question. While we are looking at Mr. Simovic's statement, sir, I'd like to look at what you both said about the redeployment of the Skorpions unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we look at page 2 in B/C/S, the next page in B/C/S, and page 3 in English. It's also the following page in English. In English if we look at the final paragraph on the page. In B/C/S it's the third paragraph from the bottom, I believe. Perhaps in the B/C/S if we can just scroll left a bit. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Here Mr. Simovic said: "After the killing of civilians in Podujevo, I know that the unit whose members were the perpetrators of this act was suspended from any further engagement and after a period of time, outside of my activities, it was engaged again in the MUP reserve force." Do you see that, sir, that passage?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Great. I'm just asking you at this point to remember that. Remember that passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, if we can see your statement again, if we look at 06108 once again. In fact, I think I just tendered that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Exhibit P1597.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. If we can look at page 3 of the English, page 2 of the B/C/S. It's the last paragraph.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Here once again, sir, it says: "After the killing of civilians in Podujevo, I know that the unit whose members were the perpetrators of this act was suspended from any further engagement and after a period of time, outside any of my activities, it was engaged again in the MUP reserve force." Do you agree, sir, that those paragraphs are identical?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is my statement, the statement I gave. I am aware of the fact that they were turned back after this incident. They were excluded from any engagement, and after awhile they were again re-engaged as the reserve force of the MUP. So what I stated here is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, again just focusing on this statement that you gave. Is it a coincidence, sir, that several items appear word for word the same in your two statements, or did Mr. Simovic and yourself sit down together, perhaps the two of you or perhaps with a third party, and come up with an account of what to say?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prosecutor, I never agreed or discussed with anyone what to say. This statement was taken by the Working Group of the ministry operating at that time, and it is exactly as is written here, the members of this reserve unit were suspended. That's what I stated on that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to ask you some question just moving to a somewhat different topic with respect to the materials that you reviewed before you testified here today. Did you have a chance, sir, before you testified here, to review Mr. Djordjevic's testimony?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And did you speak with anyone, sir, anyone who had any interest in this case prior to testifying here today, in fact, prior to you beginning your testimony yesterday about your evidence or about this case?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not speak with anyone about my evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: There were a couple of things, sir, that struck me as somewhat unusual about the evidence that you've recently given. I'd like to give you a chance to respond. Just earlier today, sir - I can give my friend the reference, it was at page 13, line 20 of today's transcript - you were asked if you had seen Mr. Djordjevic in 1999, and you responded -- in your answer you said: "Well, at least I think it was in 1999." And then you went on to provide the exact date that you saw him on, which I would note was the same date that Mr. Djordjevic gave us. Did you have any assistance, sir, in remembering that date, January 16th, that you gave us?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, I know that it was only once that -- once in 1999 that General Vlastimir Djordjevic was in Kosovo and that I provided police officers from my unit to guard these republican authorities, and I recall that it was on the 16th that I got a call from him that he was going to Kopaonik mountain. He had arrived by plane, and some sort of transportation needed to be organised. And as I said, I also wanted to go skiing, and I said I would organise the transport.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That is fine. I'll go through that testimony with you as well, but what I'm curious about, sir, is that specific date, and just to put the question to you again, you seem to have gone from not even being sure what year this was to being able to pin-point the exact date that you were with Mr. Djordjevic, and I'm asking, you did you have any assistance in remembering that it was that date? What helped you to recall that it was exactly January 16th ten years ago?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since he was there only once, and I am a commander of the special unit and I remember it was a weekend, I know he was going skiing, and I know for sure, and I claim with full responsibility that it was on the 16th of January. I know for a fact that he asked me to transfer him on the 16th of January. It was a weekend, we went skiing, and I know I went back to my base on the 17th January, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Is there any document, sir, that you saw that contained the date the 16th of January, or did somebody speak to you about the date the 16th of January?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never seen any document regarding either the 15th or the 16th of January. It's just that I know that this session was held then. I remember the session, and I remember it was the 16th when he asked me to get him to Kopaonik.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I notice that when you were testifying again previously today, when my learned friend was questioning you, when you gave the date of the 16th, you slipped twice and, in fact, you said it was the 15th then you changed it to the 16th. I see again today just now you said the 15th or the 16th. Sir, what is the significance of January 15th?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now and when I was questioned by the other lawyer, I'm saying that there was a session held at that time on the 15th and the 16th, and it was on the 16th that the chief of sector assistant minister asked me to get him to Mount Kopaonik on that skiing trip, and I said I wanted to join him. It was on the 16th for sure, and I remember that on that date I went to Mount Kopaonik.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. The question has already been answered, but my objection had to do with the way the question was asked because what the witness said just now and earlier contained no wavering between the 15th and the 16th, so my objection had to do with the evidence he gave earlier today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I think I can move on, Your Honours, but I think the transcript speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, this session you are referring to taking place on the 15th and 16th, can you explain what that was?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a session of the government of the Republic of Serbia held in Pristina and places around Kosovo, and it was finished on the 16th, and after the session was over, the chief asked me to organise transport and get him to Mount Kopaonik.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: But the 16th is the date that you saw Mr. Djordjevic, according to you; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He called me on the telephone on the 16th, and then I organised my own car and the escort to go as far as Zvecani, the escort was concerned, and the two of us went on to Kopaonik and the date was the 16th.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine. Sir, are you aware of the significance of the date of January 15th, 1999? What of significance took place that day? And I should say, what of significance to the events in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what happened on that day. All I know is that on that day after I was called, I transferred the chief of the sector, General Vlastimir Djordjevic to Kopaonik.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Are you aware of the Racak incident, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not familiar with the incident in Racak.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: You've never heard of it? Never heard about anything happening in Racak on the 15th of January?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 16th I certainly didn't know anything about it, but later when I returned from Kopaonik, I watched television and learned from the media that something happened in Racak. That's after my return from Kopaonik, so on the 16th, I wasn't aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So when you said about 30 seconds ago, no, I'm not familiar with the incident in Racak, what did you mean by that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You, you asked me, Are you aware of the incident on the 16th. I did not know of any incident, but I learned when I returned from Kopaonik. I watched it on television. There was some conference regarding the event. It was maybe the 17th, I'm not sure. But I know I watched it on television.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to ask you about another piece of your testimony. This is from yesterday, and just so we're clear, I'll take you to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we could look at yesterday's testimony. It's T13776.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: This will be in English in the transcript, sir, but I'll read it to you, so you'll receive the translation. I'll start from line 10. Sir, you were asked in chief: "When Zivko Trajkovic informed you of the need of this greater engagement, did he also propose how to deal with the situation especially in view of the fact of the number of people you had?" And, sir, you went on to discuss what Mr. Trajkovic, things that Mr. Trajkovic did and then told you. So you said: "At that meeting, he told us that he would see to it that a reserve force be found. Indeed, later on he told us that he had spoken to Mrgud whom he had known from Eastern Slavonia, Baranja, and Sermia, which I think is perhaps Western Srem, about that reserve force. Apparently Mrgud told him he knew of the people who could make part of that MUP reserve force. After that, Trajkovic informed the chief of the sector about the fact that he located a number of reservists who could be made part of the unit. He also said that Mr. Vlastimir Djordjevic, the sector chief, told him that the minister's decision still awaited on the issue of joining the MUP by the reserve force." Do you recall saying that yesterday, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very long passage that you've just read. Like I said yesterday --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: All I'm asking you -- I'm not asking you about the content, I'm just asking you simply now, do you remember saying that yesterday? I'm not asking you if it's true, I'm just asking if you remember saying it?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said yesterday that Zivko Trajkovic had spoken to Mrgud --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I don't need you to repeat it. In fact, perhaps I'll just move on, we have the transcript. What I want to ask you about that passage, sir, is that it strikes me that in that passage you are showing a remarkable memory for a conversation that you had more than ten years ago. And if we look specifically at what you are saying in that paragraph, sir, you are relating details of things that Mrgud told Trajkovic that he had told Djordjevic. You are also talking about things that Trajkovic told you that Djordjevic said about the minister. My question for you, sir, is: Are you saying today that you are able to independently remember all of those things from a conversation that took place ten years ago?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, it's the usual procedure. It all happened that way at the time, and I remember it and I should always be able to remember that when admission into the reserve force of the MUP is concerned, when Zivko Trajkovic said that a reserve force could join us, of course, he had had to tell the chief of the sector that there is this possibility and that he had to await the minister's decision on their admission. Of course, that's the usual procedure. It has nothing to do with the length of time that passed since. It was the normal procedure whenever reservists were engaged through the administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: But, sir, we are not just talking here about a usual procedure. You purported in your testimony to remember specific details about what was told to you by Mr. Trajkovic about conversations with a number of people, and these were specific conversations with specific people about specific events. What I'm asking you, sir, is, are you saying that you are able to remember all of that detail? Do you remember your conversation with Trajkovic so well that you can say that all of those things you've told us are accurate?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember that conversation the way I stated here, that Trajkovic conveyed these things. Now, whether I would be able to repeat at every moment what exactly was said, but I remember, I'm still saying that that is what Trajkovic said. That's what he conveyed to us concerning the engagement of this reserve force of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I think one can't help but notice that the evidence you related in that passage would seem to line up very well with the talking points of Mr. Djordjevic's Defence. What I'd like to ask you, sir, is, did you specifically make that statement? Did you specifically recollect those conversations in order to help Mr. Djordjevic's Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not discuss the details and what I said here about the information provided to us by Mr. Trajkovic, I didn't share these details with anyone except yesterday when I was giving evidence before this Court. I said what I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Let's move to a different topic, sir. Going back to Podujevo. After this massacre was committed and after those women and children had been shot, what happened to the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When these were killed, it's not the Skorpions, please, it's a reserve force of the MUP. When these civilians were killed, Simovic -- I don't know what happened on the spot except what Markovic informed me, namely that a car was needed to transport these people to the hospital, and when he came back, he informed me that there were dead people there, and Simovic --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Let me stop you. Let me just focus the question very specifically. What happened to these Skorpions or this MUP reserve unit? Did they remain in Podujevo, or were they sent back, and can you explain how that happened? First let me ask you, did they remain in Podujevo after the incident?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After the incident they stayed in Podujevo for another half an hour. Simovic told Medic when he came to the staff that he should go back with the reservists to Prolom Banja, and they were sent back to Prolom Banja on the same date, that is on the 28th of March, 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Did Mr. Simovic order the Skorpions to go back to Prolom Banja, Skorpions or the MUP reserve force? Did Mr. Simovic order them back to Prolom Banja?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Simovic instructed not the Skorpions, but Slobodan Medic, aka Boca, and I was present there at the relocated OUP Podujevo staff. He instructed him to get the reserve forces together and to send them back to Prolom Banja from where he had taken him early the previous morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Why did Mr. Simovic make that order?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Taken them early the previous morning.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that Mr. Simovic has issued an order to Boca to the effect of returning the reserve forces of the MUP of Republika Serbia because some members of the reserved forces had committed the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So Mr. Simovic was aware of that? Are you aware that Mr. Simovic was aware of that, sir, that a crime had been committed?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He only said that the reservists that had been brought committed the crime and that these particular reserve forces of the MUP of Republika Serbia were to be sent back to Prolom Banja.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, my objection refers to the transcript. In order to avoid some later misunderstanding, this refers to line 17 where it states that the witness said "early the previous morning," this may create confusion. I think that the witness corrected himself and said particularly which morning he meant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Behar, do you want to follow that up?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I'm not sure I see the issue. I see both times it says earlier the previous morning. I'm not sure it's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Leave it for Mr. Popovic in re-examination then, if you are not concerned.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Right. I think I understand the issue, and I don't see a problem with it, and certainly my friend is free to explore it if he does.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, if we can look at a statement you gave once again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: This is 06118 once again. The English is K054-6915. Actually, if we could look at page 36 in the B/C/S, in the English page 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I want to look at the final line here. You just told us that Mr. Simovic ordered the Skorpions, or the MUP reserve force as you are now calling it, to go back to Prolom Banja, but if we look here at this statement, I'll just read you the last lines, you say -- you said: "I really don't know why the Skorpions unit was sent back to Prolom Banja on the same day. I'm not familiar with that, because, as I said, I belonged to a completely different unit, which was under my command." Do you recall saying that, sir? And again, I'm not asking you what happened, I'm asking you, do you remember making that statement?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I gave a statement in Prokuplje but I reiterate that it's not about my not knowing about it. They were a different unit, as I said, the reserve force of the MUP of Republic of Serbia that came on that day and the special unit were two different formations. As for why this unit was sent back, I was present at this meeting at the relocated staff when Commander Simovic ordered Boca to take them back to Prolom Banja. I was present there. But again, I don't know. As I said, I haven't seen this statement. At the time when I gave it, I didn't read it, and I didn't sign it. So I claim with full responsibility that the truth is that I knew that they had been sent back precisely because of the crime they had committed, and that is why Simovic told Boca to do that on that day when we were at the meeting at the staff premises.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we can just look at the -- quickly look at the next page in English. Perhaps it's not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, let me just take you right back then to be as specific I can about what you said in that statement. Perhaps we can go back in the English again. The very first thing you said in that line, sir is: "I really don't know why the Skorpions unit was sent back to Prolom Banja." You just told us today why it was sent back. You told us that you knew Mr. Simovic made that order. My question to you, sir, is: Did you intentionally lie to the court in Prokuplje?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Prosecutor, as I said before, I know, I know that this unit was sent back because of the crime that it committed on that day, and I categorically claim that I was present when Mr. Simovic ordered for them to be sent back because these reservists of the MUP did something, and I claim with full responsibility that this is the truth what I'm telling you now, it's not that I didn't know. Quite the contrary, I knew about that, however, I did not read this statement, I did not sign it, and I don't know anything about this -- its content. I see it for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, did you yourself go back with this Skorpion or MUP reserve unit to Prolom Banja? Did you accompany them?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't accompany them when they went to Prolom Banja. After this unit was told to go to Prolom Banja, they complied, but I remained in -- there. Zoran Simovic was the one who went with them. He escorted them to Prolom Banja, which is not far away from Podujevo. I did not escort these men to Prolom Banja.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
