utterances.text: Did Mr. Simovic ask you to go with them to Prolom Banja?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I remember, I don't know. He didn't ask me to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Because yesterday, sir, or actually, on Monday --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Perhaps we can look at that. This is the testimony of 19th of April at T-13588.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we look at line 13, this is what Mr. Simovic said about that, sir. I'll just read it, so you'll receive the translation. Mr. Simovic said: "Once I had organised those ambulances for the wound, I was told that there were fatalities, and I decided to take back that reserve unit to Prolom Banja. I issued an order to my own unit members that they take back to the bus everyone they catch, and when I met up with Mr. Stalevic, I told him to go back with that reserve unit to Prolom Banja." Is that true, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm saying with full responsibility that Simovic didn't tell me to go to Prolom Banja. The statement that I gave -- every time I made a statement about that day, I said that I was at the headquarters and that Simovic informed Boca about what happened and that it was Simovic who escorted this unit to Prolom Banja. I definitely did not leave the Podujevo OUP on that day, or rather the relocated headquarters. I remained there with men from both units. When I say "units," I'm talking about Belgrade and Pristina's SAJs. After that event, pursuant to Simovic's order, the reserve forces were sent back to Prolom Banja.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: What did Mr. Simovic do with those MUP reservists when he returned them to Prolom Banja?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. Can you please repeat it. I don't think I heard it properly.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Certainly. You told us that Mr. Simovic returned with the MUP reservists to Prolom Banja. What I'm asking you is, what happened when they returned? What did Mr. Simovic do when he took them back?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When he came to the headquarters, he notified the Podujevo OUP about the crime they had committed. After that when he told Boca to get people ready to be returned and after he had informed the MUP in Kosovo and Metohija, he sent the men back to Prolom Banja, to the point where he had taken them from on the previous day.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: But, you said that Mr. Simovic took them back. Am I understanding that correctly, did he go back with them?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: After sending the notification, he came to the headquarters and he instructed Boca to take the reserve forces back. He informed the command, the staff for the Kosovo and Metohija. After the reservists set off, he went in his own car towards Prolom Banja first and then further on towards Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So that's what I'm asking you about, sir. When Mr. Simovic went with the reservists to Prolom Banja, what happened? Did you find out, and I suspect you would find out from him from speaking to him, what did he do in Prolom Banja?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He took the reserve forces to Prolom Banja. He notified the MUP staff, and then he left for Belgrade to attend the funeral of his late fellow officer Radovan Aleksic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: He also notified Mr. Djordjevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The reserve forces of the MUP were returned to Prolom Banja. Simovic should have informed General Djordjevic as well. Whether he did that or not, I really don't know. I don't know what Simovic did in the aftermath.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And can you explain why he should have informed General Djordjevic?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the reservists who were sent to us were sent immediately back to Prolom Banja after the crime. Therefore, they went to the territory of Republic of Serbia. They were no longer in the territory of Kosovo and Metohija. They were sent back to Serbia, and we should have sent information to that effect in view of what happened in Podujevo. They were again put at the motel where we had put them, and the organs in charge should have undertaken measures to discover and detect the perpetrators of the crime.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay, sir, let's take a bit of a step back here. I'm going to ask you some more general questions about the SAJ. Now, the SAJ was part of the public security department; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The special anti-terrorist unit of the MUP belonged to the Ministry of Interior, and at the time it was part of the public security department.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And General Djordjevic was the chief or the head of the public security department; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And if you needed something, if the SAJ needed something, equipment, materiels, weapons, more men, or guidance, it was General Djordjevic that your unit would approach; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not my unit, but the commander of the SAJ would approach the chief of the department if he needed any equipment or anything else. That is to say, Zivko Trajkovic, the commander of SAJ. It was not up to me to communicate with the head of the department because I had my commander above me who reported directly to the chief of the department. And I reported to my commander Zivko Trajkovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Right, and I understand there's a hierarchy, there's a chain of command. You report to Trajkovic, Mr. Trajkovic reports to Mr. Djordjevic, when you need any of those things I just mentioned; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand your question. This is the regular way in which SAJ operated. I don't know what you are asking me about. Trajkovic was with us, and it was him to whom we relayed problems that my unit might have with supplies, equipment, training, et cetera. According to this logic, it was Trajkovic who should pass on this information to the head of the department. And that exclusively referred to training and providing equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay. I think that's clear, sir. I'd like to look at some of the operations that your unit was involved in.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And if we could look at P886, please. And I'll need page 57 in English, page 59 in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, this is a record of meetings of the Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija. These are minutes that were taken for the 23rd of August, 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I see that the B/C/S is upside down. There we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I just want to ask you about what Mr. Djordjevic said. Really, sir, I'll go through it with you and then I'll have a specific question. You'll see here, sir, that General Djordjevic is speaking at this Joint Command meeting. He refers to a number of -- a number of MUP units, the 3rd MUP detachment continue activities around Sedlari, the 2nd detachment, the 1st detachment, then the special units should proceed to Duga and link up with Javor and Klecka. Do you see he is giving this whole range of instructions, sir, with respect to different forces, different detachments? What I want to ask you about, sir, is at the very bottom, it says, he says: "Conclusion: The Prizren and Belgrade companies and the SAJ, special anti-terrorist unit, to proceed along the Dulje-Rance direction." You see that there? I see you are nodding. So I'll ask you, sir, do you recall being present in that area? In other words, do you recall being present along the Dulje-Rance axis at this time, it would be in late August of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot remember exactly now whether I was there or not. It was a long time ago, but from this document, I absolutely cannot see anything. It is totally illegible. I've never seen a document of this kind specifying that I had this particular task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's fine. As long as you can understand, I suppose, sir, what I read to you, which I know is interpreted. But with respect to Dulje-Rance and whether your unit was there, am I understanding correct, you may have been but you are not sure? Is that fair?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible that I was there. We are talking about 1998, so it was possible that I was at Dulje, but I've never seen something like this. I really cannot find my bearings in this document, and I cannot see what my task would be stemming from this document. I can assure you that I never received such a task. I used to receive a map with axis plotted in it, but something like this was never specifically said to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I understand that, sir. These are actually just notes from a meeting that Mr. Djordjevic was at but I wanted to ask you about the content, and I think you've answered that. Let me move to Mr. Djordjevic's presence in the field in 1998. You spoke already today about Mr. Djordjevic in the field. For my friend, the reference is page 12, line 3. You said you were at Malisevo -- sorry, you said that Mr. Djordjevic was with you in the field in Malisevo between Pristina and Pec and at Cicavica. Are you able to remember any other times when Mr. Djordjevic was with you in the field, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, when we were unblocking the road during those summer actions, I said that I saw him on that occasion on the Lapusky-Kievo-Pec [phoen] road, and we removed those roadblocks at that time. The second time I saw him was when we were entering Malisevo, and I don't recall the date, the exact date, I saw him at the foot of Mount Cicavica. So during these combat operations, I saw quite a few refugees there, and as I said, it was in a field where these people were, we gave them food and water from our own supplies. After that my doctor, Markovic, said Governor, there's a heavily pregnant woman and if you would please provide a vehicle to take her to Pristina. And I did so. So, as I said, I saw him on a number of occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Was Mr. Djordjevic there with the SAJ, or was he co-ordinating the personnel -- the MUP personnel more generally? Let me be clear, was he there with the SAJ?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was with my SAJ. The Belgrade SAJ, there was Tetinac as well, and there was another unit from Novi Sad. Commander Zivko Trajkovic commanded the SAJ. General Vlastimir Djordjevic used to come to visit the units, not only SAJ units but also PJP units to see whether they needed anything, how things were going on, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I see. If we could look at P889, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, this is an order of the Pristina Corps Command from the 16th of February, 1999. You can see it's an order, just reading it, calling for the elimination of Albanian terrorist forces in the sector of Malo Kosovo, Drenica, and Malisevo?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we look at page 5 in B/C/S and page 6 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, just under heading number 5 there, you see where it says "task", you'll see there, sir, it calls for a co-ordinated action between the VJ and the PJP and the SAJ. Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that, the reference to the SAJ of the MUP. I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, what I want to ask you, sir, is do you remember participating in that co-ordinated action? Were you there on the ground, and do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I took part with my unit in that area, but as for the assignment in this form, it's not an assignment to my unit. We just received extracts from topographic maps. I have never seen this before.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: No, I understand that. I just wanted to ask you about your involvement on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Let's look now at P85.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, sir, these are the minutes of a MUP staff meeting in Pristina that took place on the 17th of February, 1999. And we can see right at the top of the document, the meeting was attended by Minister Stojiljkovic, Mr. Djordjevic, Rade Markovic, Obrad Stevanovic, also all members of the MUP staff including Mr. Lukic, all SUP chiefs, and PJP, and SAJ commanders, in fact, SAJ detachment commanders. Do you recall being present at this meeting, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's certain that I did not attend this meeting. I see it's written here that all members of the staff attended, and as soon as it says that MUP staff attended, it's certain that I did not because I was not a member of the staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: But, in fact, sir, many more people attended -- many people attended this meeting, and if you look at the top, it specifically says, and SAJ, or special anti-terrorist unit, detachment commanders. And the SAJ detachment commanders at this time, according to you, sir, were only yourself and Mr. Simovic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you see, when you read this it reads clearly, members of the staff, Zivko Trajkovic was a member of the staff. And at these meetings, Simovic and I had absolutely no need to attend because our units were small and there was no need. That's why Zivko Trajkovic was appointed as a member of the staff for combatting terrorism in Kosovo. I did not attend this meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Well, let's move to look at the content, sir. If we look at -- just staying on the first page about two-thirds of the way down. Unfortunately, it's one long paragraph, but there's a line -- maybe we can just scroll both pages down to the bottom. Mr. Lukic says: "A plan of the RJB, public security department, has been worked out..." do you see that, where he says "a plan of the RJB has been worked out"? Towards the bottom in the B/C/S, sir.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't see it. Where is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Let me just read it then, sir. You'll receive the translation. Mr. Lukic says: "A plan of the RJB has been worked out to prevent and thwart the entry of NATO troops into our territory." Then he says: "The staff plans, when it is ordered, to carry out three mopping-up operations in the Podujevo, Dragobilja, and Drenica areas, but was waiting for an order to do so." Do you see that, sir, or do you at least understand as you received the translation?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you've just read, I understood in interpretation, but I did not attend meeting, and I don't know what Sreten Lukic said there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Let me ask you more specifically, sir, do you recall participating in those mop-up operations in Podujevo, Dragobilja, and Drenica, in those areas?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said that I had taken part in operations, actions, but not actions of mopping up. I said I took part in that action when combat began in Malo Kosovo and that's precisely Bradas village and the area I've been talking about from the beginning. I was there with my unit in 1999. And I think it was the 24th, 25th, 26th, 27th March when the air-strikes began. My unit was involved in the work to destroy terrorist groups in villages Palatna, Metohija, Bradas, that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay. Let's follow along then. If we look at page 4 in the B/C/S and page 3 in English. Now, this is the Minister Stojiljkovic is putting forward a number of forthcoming tasks for everyone in the MUP. And you we'll see one of them towards the end, I'll just point this out to you, sir, one of them is "more effective inclusion and engagement of the SAJ." It's the third from the bottom. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that. I can see that written.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So this would have been not long before, as you've just described, the Podujevo operation and those other operations that you went to perform, correct? This is mid-February and what you were talking about was towards the end of March?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here at this meeting it was said that the unit should be better and more deeply engaged because NATO air-strikes against our country were about to begin, and it's a conclusion of this meeting that we should get involved, we should be more engaged in these actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, another -- another point forthcoming task that the minister puts out here, sir, I believe it's the 12th from the top, if you can count down, this is what I'd like your comment on. He says, the minister says: "Approach and engage volunteers carefully, linking their engagement through the reserve police force when assessed as necessary." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I'm not sure if it's on that page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Perhaps we can go back a page in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: It should be actually at the bottom.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Right. I'll just read it again one more time so we are clear. "Approach and engage volunteers carefully, linking their engagement through the reserve police force when assessed as necessary." Do you follow that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's written here, but I don't know who said this, and I did not attend this meeting anyway, so I can't know what was said there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Well, the minister said it, and if we could scroll back one page in the B/C/S, you can see it, and in the English.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. It says "engage volunteers" in this passage. We, the special anti-terrorist unit, never had any volunteers, and the ministry never had any volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: That's, in fact, just what I wanted to ask you, sir, because in fact, engaging volunteers into the police was not allowed, was it?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the police does not have any volunteers. At that time in the police we only had reserve forces of the MUP. Certainly not volunteers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And to go the one step further, sir, in fact, using volunteers in the police would be contrary to law, would it not?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to our regulations in the ministry, we don't have volunteers. Volunteers do not exist. We never had any. I can only answer to that. As for the rest, we never had any reserve force in the MUP. Sorry, sorry, I made a mistake, we didn't have any volunteer units, and volunteer units do not exist in the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So I guess what I'm putting to you, sir, is it would not be legal to simply engage a bunch of volunteers, put them in a uniform and then insert them into the police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I maintain with full responsibility that we did not have any volunteers within our reserve force. We did not have any volunteers among reservists. There were reservists engaged by the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, namely the administration for the police of the Ministry of the Interior. They were the reserve force. That was organised by the MUP, and we did not have volunteers ever.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we can look at P356, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, sir, this is a dispatch that was sent from Mr. Djordjevic to all SUPs, to the MUP staff, and to a number of others, as you'll see at the top of the page there. You can see this was sent out the very next day following the meeting that I just showed you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Perhaps we can just very quickly look at the final page, and I'll show you that it does indeed come from Mr. Djordjevic. Now, if we could look at page 2 in the B/C/S and page 3 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Looking at point number 7, very top of the English and towards the bottom in the B/C/S, Mr. Djordjevic says: "Through intensified intelligence and other measures and actions, carry out the necessary checks, compile lists, and establish complete control over volunteer and paramilitary units and their members." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So it would appear from this, sir, that Mr. Djordjevic is looking to make use of volunteers and paramilitary units and for the ministry to exert control over them. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't agree with that. I've never seen this before. And anyway, I can't see the statement, which you are referring to, concerning complete control over volunteer and paramilitary units. I maintain with full responsibility that the Ministry of Interior never had a paramilitary or a volunteer unit in the force where I worked.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: What were the Skorpions, sir? Were the Skorpions not a paramilitary unit?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Skorpions, emphasising again, when they came to us, they were a reserve unit of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia engaged in conformity with the prevailing procedure. The minister had made a decision, and they were sent to us to Prolom Banja. They were brought to us and turned back the same day, and the second time around when Zivko Trajkovic brought them, they were part of our unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I understand well that they were made part of your unit. My question for you is, were the Skorpions a paramilitary unit?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the Skorpions were a reserve force of the MUP engaged by the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Okay. Then let me put it somewhat differently --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic has been waiting patiently.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I actually have three objections in one. First of all, the witness has never at any moment mentioned Skorpions in his evidence, and to put words in his mouth as to what kind of unit they were is not based on his evidence. Second, when the witness is shown documents, the first thing to be asked is whether he knows anything about the document because if we look at the first page, we'll see this document had never been made available to his unit. And, third, we should also take care to -- of the extent to which this unit can be helpful concerning legislation and certain other matters that are being brought up now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I make the observation, Mr. Popovic, that this is cross-examination. It's not examination-in-chief. He may be asked if a Skorpion unit was a paramilitary unit. He has no bother, as I've listened to his evidence, in answering that question just as the reference to Skorpions appears many times in statements that he has made. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, to re-approach this issue with the Skorpions, what I want to ask you is, were the Skorpions a known paramilitary unit before they became part of the MUP reserve force?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, they were not. Before they came in, I did not know them as Skorpions. In 1999, I knew them as a reserve force of the MUP when they came to join us, and I did not know of any earlier name they had had maybe from before.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Knowing what you know now, sir, today, do you accept that the Skorpions were a paramilitary unit before they joined the MUP reserve force?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before they joined the reserve force of the MUP, I was never aware that they had been a paramilitary unit. I know that once they joined, they were the reserve force of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I'm saying, sir, knowing what you know today, what you know now, would you agree that the Skorpions were a paramilitary unit before they joined the MUP reserve force?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm just saying about the period when they joined us, that was a reserve unit of the MUP, a reserve unit of the Ministry of the Interior that had undergone the procedure of approval to be attached as our reserve.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I don't think I am getting an answer, sir, but I see we are at the time for the break. I'm in the hands of the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll have the second break now and we resume at 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Behar.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Welcome back, sir. I want to spend the remainder of our day talking somewhat more generally about the SAJ. Now, members of the SAJ were normally selected from amongst the ranks of regular police through a vetting process; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Members of the SAJ were selected from amongst the best police officers within the then-secretariats. Very often we would choose members from the secondary school of the interior in Sremska Kamenica after a year or two of schooling if they proved to be good. They were most often good students, good athletes, and they had good physical -- physical characteristics that would be suitable for the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And you, in fact, had recruiters that would look closely at the mental and the physical capacities and qualities of any potential candidate for the SAJ; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a single candidate could be admitted unless first we have completed all the physical checks with them, medical examinations, and other tests. After that, they would undergo training and I would take part in the selection process. Only after that, if they proved to be satisfactory during training, could they become members of the special anti-terrorist unit of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. So only and exclusively such candidates would be admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And then once these candidates were admitted and into the SAJ, then they were, in fact, intensively trained; correct? You had a significant amount of training for all of your SAJ members?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the standard training according to plans for the SAJ including the recruitment and selection of members of the SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Is it fair to say, sir, that you regarded yourself within the SAJ as the best of the best from within the MUP?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it would be immodest for me to say that. As I said yesterday in my evidence, I was sent from the SAJ as a police officer because I was a good student at the military academy, and as such, I was admitted into the SAJ. In my opinion, I think I was good, but I cannot say that I was the best of them. However, I was the commander of the SAJ of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia in Pristina.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, I heard that one of the mottos or saying that the SAJ had was, we train for years for a job that takes seconds to complete. Are you familiar with that? Was that something you've heard?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've never heard such a saying. We were being trained for every-day tasks. As much as we were trained, we were capable of providing the performance that was incorporated in what you are saying and you are citing. It is true that we were an elite unit, that we were well trained, and that we were capable to act as an elite unit of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Well, I read that quote in a long article written about the SAJ, but what I took it to reflect, sir, was the difficulty of the job that your unit has to do. And, in fact, you carry weapons that have great destructive force, and it's not safe, certainly, for just anyone to be walking around with weapons of that strength; would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question as you put it. I didn't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Let me put it again, sir. The reason for all of this great selection and care into who gets into the SAJ, and the reason for all this training for your men is because you do, in fact, a very difficult and a very delicate job. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The training of our police officers was specific. As I said yesterday, as a unit, we were intended to combat terrorism, to be involved in the incidents of disturbance of public law and order to a greater extent, including hijacking of planes and other transportation means, and we had to undergo high-quality training for that, and we had high-quality members in the SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And as members of the SAJ, sir, you carry powerful weapons that could, in fact, if in the wrong hands or if not handled responsibly, could be very dangerous; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't have what you are saying we had. Our people were trained to handle weapons. They were well prepared for every possible task, and I was always with them, so it could never happen that they might abuse the weapons that you are mentioning, so they were well trained for the tasks that they were expected to carry out. That is why we trained them, that is why we had medical checks, psychological checks, all kinds of tests that have to be carried out with a unit of that kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, with all of this careful selection, with all of this training for your SAJ member, what I have trouble understanding is that when you have these men, these men who call themselves the Skorpions, within minutes of getting off of the bus for their very first deployment gathered up unarmed civilians including women and children and use those weapons issued to them to kill, to kill civilians. What I have trouble understanding, sir, is how men of this calibre could be integrated into your elite SAJ unit?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You asked me several questions here. SAJ was an elite unit. This reserve force of the MUP that you mentioned was never part of the SAJ. They were MUP reserve forces, and I was talking about the SAJ and police members of a special anti-terrorist unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Well, we heard quite clearly yesterday, sir, from Mr. Simovic, that the intention was to join them up with the SAJ, and, in fact, that was being concluded, according to him, right before the massacre took place, so regardless, and we may not agree on that, but it's clear that the intention was always for them to join the SAJ unit; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not right. They were brought there as the MUP reserve forces, and they were brought to Podujevo. They were not included in our reserve forces of our units. They were not attached to our units. After this crime, Mr. Simovic ordered Boca to return them from where they had come from, that is to say, to Prolom Banja.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: But then some weeks later, sir, they were, in fact, incorporated into your SAJ unit; correct? Were they not redeployed to the SAJ?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not deployed in the SAJ. When they returned a few weeks later, the proposal of Zivko Trajkovic remained the reserve force of the MUP. Upon their arrival in late April, they were divided between me and Simovic, and part of that unit was incorporated in our further tasks. So only second time around when they arrived, Zivko Trajkovic, the commander gave a number of men to me and to the commander of the Belgrade SAJ. We provided billeting headquarters for those men. We checked what their military specialties were, and after this -- the reserve forces of the MUP were attached to us, we proceeded with carrying out the tasks that were assigned to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So they were then, incorporated into the SAJ. But let me ask you this, sir, is it fair to say that these mean, these MUP reservists and self-named Skorpions, had absolutely no business being armed, uniformed, transported, and then joined up with your highly trained SAJ units? Is that a fair comment, sir, that they did not belong in the ranks of the SAJ?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very long question, and you are at the same time providing an answer. I'm telling you those were reserve forces of the Serbian MUP, which pursuant to the then-MUP minister, Vlajko Stojiljkovic, were engaged, or rather, admitted into the reserve force, and it was supposed to be attached to us on the 28th when Tetinac or rather, Simovic brought them to Podujevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Let me ask you this more directly, sir. In your view, was it irresponsible to take these men and incorporate them into the MUP reserve unit? You know your men, you know these men, in your view, was it irresponsible?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My opinion is with regard to this and to readmittance is the following: Zivko Trajkovic, the then-commander of --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat the title of Mr. Zivko Trajkovic. The interpreters didn't catch that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, we didn't get the interpretation after you said something about Zivko Trajkovic. If you could perhaps just repeat your answer again. You said my opinion is with regard to this, and to readmittance is the following: Zivko Trajkovic, then if you could just repeat your answer, please.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Zivko Trajkovic guaranteed that these men would carry out their tasks in an extremely responsible and professional way once they were admitted into the reserve forces of MUP when he brought them to Kosovo Polje second time around which took place in late April.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Well, sir, would one person guaranteeing something give you as a professional enough confidence that men who had been involved in an incident as serious as that massacre could be trusted once again to be? deployed?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, and I would like to underline that, Commander Trajkovic or special units of MUP of the Republic of Serbia guaranteed for these men that they would act in an honourable and professional way. Why should I not believe my commander that that wouldn't be the case?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we could see D401, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, sir, the obligation for your men to be qualified was, in fact, directly stated in this decision that governs the existence of the SAJ. If we can look at paragraph number 2. So this is the decision that established the SAJ. And paragraph number 2 it says: "It shall also be the task of the SAJ to maintain the necessary level of professional and mental and physical fitness of its members for carrying out tasks and responsibilities from Article 1 of this item in accordance with the plan and programme for training the SAJ." So do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, sir, would it be possible to incorporate a bunch of men into your unit without knowing at all what their qualifications were? In other words, let me be more specific about that, sir. Before anyone was going to incorporate some men into the MUP reserve and then into your unit to fight with the SAJ, the person doing that would need to know who they were, what they had been doing before, what kind of weapons experience did they have, and what had happened if they had fought before, what happened when they fought before? Do you agree, sir, that the person who made the decision would need to know all of that information?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not agree with you because the decision on the reserve force was taken by the minister of the interior, and after that, the commander of the unit Trajkovic was in charge. I'm still maintaining that this was the reserve force of the MUP and not the reserve force of the special unit. The special unit had never had amongst its ranks any reserve forces. As I told you, there used to be SAJ Belgrade, SAJ Pristina, and SAJ Novi Sad, and SAJ commander Trajkovic was based in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: We can even leave aside for a moment, sir, which specific person made the decision. In fact, I'll come to that in a moment, but what I'd like you to answer is, anyone, anyone who was involved in the decision of incorporating these men into the MUP reserve, they would have to know who the men were, what they were doing, what they had been doing before, what experience they had; do you agree, sir? All these things would need to be known by the people that made that decision?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as far as this is concerned, that all should have been done by the police administration of the MUP. They should have carried out this vetting procedure. The Ministry of the Interior of Republic of Serbia could not admit anyone. I'm speaking specifically, for example, about the people with criminal record and, therefore, they would not be allowed to carry out those duties. That applied to people who had served in the military. Unless they hadn't served in the military, they couldn't be admitted into MUP. Those were some basic principles that had to be abided by when people were admitted into the reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Now, sir, if we can continue looking at this document. Let's look at paragraph number 5, if we can just scroll down in the English and the B/C/S. You can read this --

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: We need the next page in the B/C/S, I see.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So I'll read this aloud, sir, but you can read it as well on the page. It says: "The provision of Articles 4 to 6 of the regulations on job planning in the Ministry of the Interior," it goes on, "shall be applicable to questions pertaining to internships, probationary work, and exceptional assignment to posts of the SAJ after first obtaining permission from the chief of the department of public security." So, sir, there are a number of things listed there, and one of them is exceptional assignment to posts of the SAJ, and this item, sir, specifically says that first the permission needed to be obtained from the chief of the department, who was Mr. Djordjevic. Do you see that section here, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you just explain which passage. Is it number 5? Issues related to probationary work, internships. I have to explain that the word here is not members [B/C/S spoken], it's[B/C/S spoken]. That's young officers on trial period whom we took from secretariats, and I said already, we took them for testing, screening, fitness tests, psychological tests. This provision applies to them and their admission, and that means they undergo procedure before being admitted into SAJ.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I understand that, sir, and, in fact, if we look, this is talking specifically about people who are going to be brought into the SAJ, made members of the SAJ, and it says -- it deals with three questions, questions pertaining to internships, probationary work, and the last one is exceptional assignment to posts of the SAJ, and then, sir, it says: "For any of those things, permission needs to first be obtained from the chief of the department of public security." Do you follow that?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that. I've already said that. The chief of the public security department is the one who approves the plan of training, and in this period indicated here, he was the one who approved the plan and he helped us with equipment and other supplies to the unit, and as far as I can see, this paragraph applies to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And, in fact, sir, the chief of the department is the only senior leadership position that's identified in this entire document; correct? It refers to the chief of the department. There's no other reference in this document to other senior leadership positions? In fact, I don't even see any reference to the minister, sir.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the decision was adopted by the minister. It's written at the bottom of the page. But regarding this paragraph you are asking me about, it refers to young employees on trial period, trainees, et cetera. We worked in special anti-terrorist units, Pristina, Novi Sad, and Belgrade. We trained them, and we prepared them for admission into the special anti-terrorist units, and by that I mean us commanders of these three SAJ units.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Well, I agree with you, sir, that this paragraph is dealing in several respects with admission into the special anti-terrorist unit. I would point out as well, one of the things is that -- where there were to be exceptional assignments, you see that phrase, "exceptional assignments"? Any exceptional assignment to be posted to the SAJ required the permission of the chief of the department. And that was Mr. Djordjevic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't give any comment on this, and from what you see -- from what you are saying, I don't think the chief of department could do that. It was in my exclusive competence to train, to prepare people, and to propose admission into the SAJ. That's concerning my unit. The commander of the second unit did the same for his unit and the third unit the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, you've told us several times today that these men, the Skorpions, were introduced to your unit by the way of the MUP reserve. You keep referring to them as MUP reservists. So if we can, let's look at the Law of Internal Affairs and see what that says about reserves.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: If we could see P66. If we can see page 9 in the English and page 3 in the B/C/S. Page 9 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So, sir, let's look at Article 27 together, if we can. You see Article 27 there, I'll just read it. It says: "In case of an imminent" --

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment. Can we zoom in on this article. I can't really see it. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: The article says, sir: "In case of an imminent threat of war or war, the Ministry of the Interior shall be brought up to strength with conscripts from the reserve force of the ministry." And then this is what I want to ask you about, sir. The next paragraph, says: "Only conscripts meeting the requirements prescribed by the law for work in the ministry may be assigned to the reserve force of the Ministry of Interior." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: So, I take it, sir, as a commander of a unit that took on these MUP reserves, this legal provision is something you would have been aware of; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I knew that they are supposed to have completed their military service and to be conscripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: And, in fact, sir, this article specifically is catered to or directed to an imminent threat of war or war. So, in fact, this is what applies during a war or during an imminent threat of war; correct? This isn't a peacetime provision only.

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, upon admission into the reserve force of the MUP, this job was done by the administration, the relevant administration within the MUP, and they handled the entire procedure for admission of members into the reserve force.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: In fact, sir, there are a number of laws that govern qualifications, both for reservists and of course for members of the police, but I would suggest to you that one of the main reasons, if not the main reason to have those laws and regulations was to prevent the possibility that a group like this, like these self-named Skorpions, a group that contained criminals would be heavily armed by the state, would be deployed into civilian areas, and that they would kill people. Would you agree, sir, that that was one of the purposes, if not the main purpose for such laws?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree with you. They were a reserve force of the ministry, and I have to emphasise once again, that screening for these men who were admitted into this reserve force was handled by employees of the ministry. They had conducted the vetting and screening, both looking into records and checking that they had done their military service.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, was the fact that these men were admitted into the MUP reserve, these men who called themselves the Skorpions, was this not a failure of the process?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When these people joined the reserve force of the ministry, from that moment on, I know them as the reserve force of the Ministry of the Interior, not as Skorpions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, at what point did you learn that these men were the Skorpions? At what point did you learn that it was the Skorpions who would be joining you?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not know when they were coming from the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. I did not know of any such name as the Skorpions. Long afterwards did I learn that this was the Skorpion unit. Later on. At that time I did not know. To me, as a commanding officer, they were a reserve force of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, when did you learn that they were the Skorpions? You said much later. When?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, sometime in 2002 or 2003 I learned of that name, the Skorpions. I think it was in 2002. As for the period before, Zivko Trajkovic told us at the time that he had been there and that he knew that man Mrgud.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Popovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, for the record, this is a very important point. Line 23, page 72, the witness did not say that this was the Skorpion unit. He said that some of those men were Skorpions. We can, of course, check by listening to the tapes, but since it is entered into the transcript in this language, I had to intervene now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You want that checked?

utterances.speaker: MR. POPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We'll have that done.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: Sir, you said you learned, you think, in 2002. How did you learn in 2002 that these were the Skorpions?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Then and now, I'm saying that this unit when they came to us, that was a unit from the reserve force of the MUP of the Republic of Serbia. That unit was the reserve force of the MUP of Republic of Serbia, and I really really did not know that they -- that those were Skorpions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: We have that position from you, sir. What I'm asking you is, when you did find out that they were called the Skorpions - you say it was in 2002 - how did you find out that they were the Skorpions at that time?

utterances.speaker: RADISLAV STALEVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 2002 when I was making a statement or giving evidence, I heard somebody called them or referred to them as Skorpions. That means in 2002. That year, the year in question, 1999, I did not know that they were Skorpions. I claimed for a fact that they were the reserve force of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I see we are at the break time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it the case that you are deliberately delaying tending certain matters into evidence that were considered today?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: There were some matters, which I believe I will use, the earlier 65 ter documents that I was -- I think I will use some more. I'm not sure if I've omitted to tender a recent document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: So you prefer to wait until tomorrow, is that it?

utterances.speaker: MR. BEHAR
utterances.text: I think that would be best, and I will certainly revisit and see if I've forgotten anything as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. We adjourn now. We resume at 9.00 tomorrow morning. A Court Officer will assist you during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
